slope.label: Typical slope
slope.plain: How steep the ground usually is across a 10 km patch. Rovers and builders want it gentle.

relief.label: Height range
relief.plain: Difference between the high and low ground in a 10 km patch.

safe10.label: Ground under 10°
safe10.plain: Share of the patch flatter than NASA's 10° landing limit.

flat5.label: Ground under 5°
flat5.plain: Share of the patch flat enough for pads, roads and solar farms.

strength.label: Ground strength (estimate)
strength.plain: How much load the ground can carry. Nothing measures it directly, so it is estimated from stand-in data.

rocks.label: Rock cover
rocks.plain: Share of the ground covered by boulders big enough to tip a lander.

frozen.label: Frozen months a year
frozen.plain: Months when the ground's average temperature stays below 0 °C, so ground ice can last.

ground_ice.label: Water in the ground
ground_ice.plain: How much water the top metre of ground holds, as ice or bound in minerals.

feldspar.label: Feldspar-rich rock
feldspar.plain: Share of the ground made of pale, feldspar-rich rock like the Moon's highlands, the rock a base would bake oxygen from.

hydrated.label: Clays and sulfates
hydrated.plain: Share of the ground with water-made minerals (clays, sulfates), which hold water and preserve signs of past life.

cold.label: Coldest ground temperature
cold.plain: The coldest the ground surface gets in a year. Both sides are ground temperatures, not air.

season_swing.label: Yearly temperature swing
season_swing.plain: Gap between the hottest and coldest ground temperatures of the year.

day_swing.label: Day-to-night swing
day_swing.plain: How much the temperature drops from day to night.

dry.label: Rain and snow
dry.plain: Average rain and snow. Mars gets none.

sun_height.label: Noon sun height
sun_height.plain: How high the sun gets at noon, averaged over a year. Near the Moon's south pole it skims the horizon, so shadows are long.

dust_haze.label: Dust in the air
dust_haze.plain: How hazy the air is with lifted dust, as optical depth. Compared by how much dust the wind lifts, not by wind speed, because Mars air is about 1% as thick as Earth's. Earth's value counts all airborne particles, not only dust.

bare.label: Bare ground
bare.plain: Share of the 10 km patch that is barren rock, sand or soil with no plants, from NASA's MODIS land-cover map. The Moon and Mars are entirely bare.

checks.label: Known analog beats an ordinary place
Held-out half only: beats an ordinary place

moon.note: Not passed. Haughton crater ranks top, but after review we added four cold ordinary places (Yakutsk taiga, Central Finland forest, Saskatchewan prairie, West Siberian plain), and they score as high as Mistastin and Lofoten. Cold, frozen ground and a low sun don't tell a polar analog apart from a cold farm or forest. Rock would: the Moon's highlands are feldspar-rich, but our rock values are still samples, so they are left out of this check. Teide, Mauna Kea and Lanzarote rank low, as expected for warm volcanic sites that train for the Moon's dark plains.
moon.firstRun: First run (14 Nov, each trait counted once, air temperatures): known analog beat an ordinary place in 97% of pairs.

Known analog beats a plain desert
Held-out half only: beats a plain desert

mars.note: Close, not passed on all places. Adding NASA bare-ground and dust data and counting each challenge once lifted the known analogs from 43% to 79% against ordinary places (pass mark 80%) and from 17% to 54% against plain deserts (pass mark 60%). The held-out half of the analogs, which the change was not tuned on, passes both marks (82% and 65%). Cold forests (Yakutsk, West Siberia) still score high, and three sandy deserts (Rub' al Khali, Grand Erg Oriental, Thar) beat many analogs because they are dry, bare and dusty. Minerals (clays, sulfates) would separate them, and those are still samples.
